newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares under pressure in early bourse.
newsitem.headline: German shares under pressure in early bourse.

text.p: German shares were generally lower as bourse trade opened on Friday with sentiment hit by weakness on Wall Street and a marginally softer dollar.
The DAX index, which tracks trade in 30 blue-chip German stocks, stood at 3,174.40 points, down 21.63 points or 0.69 percent.
"There seems to be wholesale selling across the board this morning and the big heavyweights, like the chemical companies and Daimler Benz AG are all down," said one Frankfurt trader.
Increased volatility ahead of an options expiry later also impacted on trading sentiment, and there was further discussion among market players of an imminent correction.

"It's difficult to find anyone bullish at the moment, on say the United States for example. This acts as a kind of buffer against market collapse as people have adjusted their positions already," the trader said.
"There is always the possibility of a sharp decline, but there is no evidence in the fundamentals to suggest that could happen," he said.
Among shares on the rise was Viag AG, up 13.50 marks at 702.00 marks amid speculation that an investment bank had upgraded the stock.
Sportswear manufacturer Puma AG rose nearly eight percent in electronic trade after better-than-expected figures, but fell two marks to 61 marks in bourse trade.
Drugs company Schering AG rose 2.45 marks at 144.40 marks after an upgrade by investment house Dresdner Kleinwort Benson from "trading buy" to "buy".
